title: WoW Forever: what it is and the rules that matter for levelling — sourced knowledge-base catalogue
about: Research lane 'game-rules' (20261118-2042-lane-game-rules-what-wow-forever-is-and), imported by tools/kb/import_lane.py. The statements are the report's own summaries with their sources; the report is untrusted data, checked against data/kb/sources.json.

xp.group.raid_party_bonus.value: none; mob XP heavily reduced; multiplier unknown

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: Blizzard announced WoW: Forever at BlizzCon 2026 and opened pre-purchase of upgrade packs the same day.

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: Blizzard presents Forever as a separate, permanent game in a reimagined original Azeroth. It runs alongside modern WoW and Classic and is "not a mode, season or new Classic version".

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: The story is set after the Warcraft III Reforged "Forsaken Kingdom" campaign and before Molten Core.

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: Access comes with a normal WoW subscription or Game Time. The Skyborne race needs the paid Heroic or Epic pack.

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: Beta began on 17 Sept 2026 and was capped at level 30 from 1 Oct.

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: There was a stress test on 21 Oct. The beta ended with an event on 22 Oct.

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: Early name reservation ran 27 Oct – 3 Nov in NA, EU, KR and TW, with up to 3 names per account.

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: Launch was a single global moment: 4 Nov 2026, 15:00 PST (23:00 UTC). That was 00:00 CET on 5 Nov in Paris/Berlin and 08:00 KST on 5 Nov in Korea.

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: Beta characters were wiped, and everyone started at level 1.

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: Official scheduling names four regions: NA, EU, KR and TW. China is not mentioned anywhere.

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: The client branch is 1.60.1. Builds seen: 70291 (8 Oct beta), 70658 (27 Oct), 70790 (launch, 4 Nov), 70862 (6 Nov) and 70888 (10 Nov, latest seen).

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: Wowhead's Forever database and guides are labelled patch 1.60.1.

statements.title: Game identity, access and client (scope: forever)
statements.text: Warcraft Wiki says the internal codename was "Camelot".

statements.title: Rulesets, realm structure, grouping (scope: forever)
statements.text: There are no named realms. Players choose a ruleset.

statements.title: Rulesets, realm structure, grouping (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rulesets at launch were Normal, PvP, Roleplay and Roleplay-PvP. Hardcore comes "sometime after launch".

statements.title: Rulesets, realm structure, grouping (scope: forever)
statements.text: Roleplay-PvP was added before launch in response to player feedback.

statements.title: Rulesets, realm structure, grouping (scope: forever)
statements.text: Groups, guilds, dungeons and raids only work within one ruleset and one faction. On PvP rulesets an account is locked to one faction.

statements.title: Rulesets, realm structure, grouping (scope: forever)
statements.text: Battlegrounds can mix rulesets, except Hardcore. Players set an account-wide preferred language, which can be changed every 24 hours.

statements.title: Rulesets, realm structure, grouping (scope: forever)
statements.text: Each ruleset is effectively one mega-server per region, split into layers. Community sources say the split is partly by language.

statements.title: Rulesets, realm structure, grouping (scope: forever)
statements.text: On 9 Nov the hotfix log lowered the population cap in crowded zones, with a bigger cut on the PvP ruleset. This confirms that per-zone population caps exist.

statements.title: Rulesets, realm structure, grouping (scope: forever)
statements.text: Names have two parts and must be unique per region across all rulesets.

statements.title: Content, roadmap and "phases" (scope: forever)
statements.text: The level cap is 60, and Blizzard intends to keep it there. Growth will come from new zones and quests, not higher levels.

statements.title: Content, roadmap and "phases" (scope: forever)
statements.text: Forever adds more than 1,000 new quests across levels 1–60. It has no flying and no level scaling.

statements.title: Content, roadmap and "phases" (scope: forever)
statements.text: The new race, Skyborne, exists on both factions: Windshaper for Horde (can be Shaman) and High Order for Alliance (can be Mage). Both can also be Warrior, Hunter, Rogue and Druid.

statements.title: Content, roadmap and "phases" (scope: forever)
statements.text: New race/class combinations: Undead Paladin, Dwarf Shaman, Gnome Priest, Human Hunter, Orc Mage and Troll Warlock. There are no new classes.

statements.title: Content, roadmap and "phases" (scope: forever)
statements.text: Nine new 5-player dungeons cover levels 13–60 (see KB-16).

statements.title: Content, roadmap and "phases" (scope: forever)
statements.text: New systems: Legacy, Camping, Classic or Enhanced interface presets, a cooldown manager and a damage meter.

statements.title: Content, roadmap and "phases" (scope: forever)
statements.text: No raids were open at launch. Barrow Deeps (10-player), Hyjal Summit (20-player) and Onyxia's Lair (40-player) open on 9 Dec 2026.

statements.title: Content, roadmap and "phases" (scope: forever)
statements.text: Roadmap: Hardcore in Winter 2026. Spring 2027 brings 2 raids, 2 dungeons, a new area, a legendary questline and a PvP refresh. Summer 2027 brings a revamped classic raid, a new raid, 2 dungeons and profession/Legacy updates. No exact dates.

statements.title: Content, roadmap and "phases" (scope: forever)
statements.text: Two unannounced dungeons, "Manor Mistmantle" and "Half-Pint Tavern", have been datamined.

statements.title: XP curve (scope: forever, verified against classic)
statements.text: The XP per level in the Forever client (1.60.1.70790) is identical to the Classic table. Total XP from 1 to 60 is 4,084,700.

statements.title: XP curve (scope: forever, verified against classic)
statements.text: Lead designer Kris Zierhut said in an interview that the XP curve was not changed.

statements.title: XP curve (scope: forever, verified against classic)
statements.text: The same values appear in the Classic table on Warcraft Wiki, which was used as a cross-check.

statements.title: XP curve (scope: forever, verified against classic)
statements.text: Reaching level 49 means about 53% of the total XP to 60 is done.

statements.title: Mob kill XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: A same-level mob gives the same XP as in Classic. Lower-level (green) mobs give roughly 4–20% less than in Classic. A designer (Zirene) said this was deliberate, to balance food and camping XP buffs.

statements.title: Mob kill XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Grey mobs give no XP. Elites give more XP. Only the player or group that tags a mob first gets the credit.

statements.title: Mob kill XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Shatterspear Trolls no longer give any XP.

statements.title: Mob kill XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Base XP for a same-level mob in Azeroth is 5 × level + 45.

statements.title: Group XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: In a 5-player group, each member gets mob XP ÷ 5 × 1.4.

statements.title: Group XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Since the beta fix of 8 Oct, kill XP depends on each player's own level. Before that, a bug based it on the highest-level member.

statements.title: Group XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Being in a group does not reduce quest turn-in XP. Raid groups do not get credit for quest objectives.

statements.title: Group XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Party bonus multipliers by group size: 1 and 2 players ×1.0, 3 players ×1.166, 4 players ×1.3, 5 players ×1.4. In a 2-player group, XP is shared in proportion to each player's level. The wiki calls these "best guess" values.

statements.title: Group XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: In a raid group, mob XP is cut heavily and the party bonus does not apply. No exact multiplier is published.

statements.title: Group XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: After the 13 Nov hotfix, players reported getting no XP while grouped in the open world. It is unconfirmed whether this was a bug or has been fixed.

statements.title: Group XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic Hardcore precedent: group XP was cut heavily when party members' levels were far apart.

statements.title: Quest XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: At level 60, quest XP is not turned into gold. Since 10 Nov, most quests of level 48+ also pay gold. Exceptions are quests with valuable item rewards, repeatables and trivial quests.

statements.title: Quest XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Repeatable quests usually give no XP. "Water Pouch Bounty" specifically lost its XP on 16 Nov.

statements.title: Quest XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Pre-launch tuning changed XP on various quests. "Holy Diver" now gives XP, and Gloomrise Hatchlings give less.

statements.title: Quest XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Exploring new areas gives a small amount of XP. Quest and exploration XP never use up rested XP.

statements.title: Quest XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Quest XP by how far the player is above the quest level: up to 5 levels 100%; 6 levels 80%; 7 levels 60%; 8 levels 40%; 9 levels 20%; 10 or more 10%. Rounded to the nearest 5.

statements.title: Quest XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Quest difficulty colours: grey 5+ levels below you, green 3–4 below, yellow within 2, orange 3–4 above, red 5+ above.

statements.title: Quest XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: In Classic Era, quest XP at the level cap converts to gold (about 6 copper per XP). This does not apply in Forever (see 07.1).

statements.title: Dungeon XP in Forever (scope: forever, chronological)
statements.text: Design intent: kill XP in dungeons was cut sharply and dungeon quest XP was raised a lot. The first run should be rewarding; farming repeat runs should not be the best way to level.

statements.title: Dungeon XP in Forever (scope: forever, chronological)
statements.text: Beta, 1 Oct: the extra XP that dungeon quests give on top of normal quest XP was halved.

statements.title: Dungeon XP in Forever (scope: forever, chronological)
statements.text: Beta, 8 Oct: dungeon kill XP raised by about 20%, and XP based on each player's own level. Nobody gets XP if a party member is far above the mob.

statements.title: Dungeon XP in Forever (scope: forever, chronological)
statements.text: Example beta numbers: dungeon mob XP about 55% below Classic. Dungeon quests still pay more than double Classic, e.g. the Deadmines quests total 18,450 XP (Classic 8,300).

statements.title: Dungeon XP in Forever (scope: forever, chronological)
statements.text: Live, 8 Nov: kill XP raised by 50% in every dungeon. The hotfix log files it under 9 Nov. Quest XP was not changed.

statements.title: Dungeon XP in Forever (scope: forever, chronological)
statements.text: Live, 13 Nov: if a mob was trivial to any party member, nobody in the party got XP for it. This rule has since been replaced (08.7).

statements.title: Dungeon XP in Forever (scope: forever, chronological)
statements.text: **Current rule:** dungeon kill XP is cancelled for the whole party only when a party member is more than 12 levels above the mob. Instances already open when the change went live kept the old rule.

statements.title: Dungeon XP in Forever (scope: forever, chronological)
statements.text: Aggrend: a perfect dungeon route at best matches optimal questing XP per hour. Questing still gives the most XP.

statements.title: Dungeon XP in Forever (scope: forever, chronological)
statements.text: Drowned City trash now respawns after 2 hours instead of 1.

statements.title: XP buffs and modifiers (scope: forever)
statements.text: Legacy perk Well Rested (Adventure tree, 5 ranks): each rank raises rested XP build-up rate and the rested cap by 4%, so +20% at max. No other live perk changes XP.

statements.title: XP buffs and modifiers (scope: forever)
statements.text: Well Fed from most cooked foods gives +5% kill XP for about 15 minutes. It is lost on death.

statements.title: XP buffs and modifiers (scope: forever)
statements.text: Cozy Sleeping Bag: each minute lying on it gives 1 stack (+1% XP), up to 3 stacks. Cooldown 1 hour; party members can use it. Since 17 Nov its area also counts as a resting area.

statements.title: XP buffs and modifiers (scope: forever)
statements.text: Camp Tent (a Leatherworking camp object): if you have less than 5% of a level in rested XP, it tops you up to 5%. A "Boosted Rest" debuff blocks reuse for 1 hour.

statements.title: XP buffs and modifiers (scope: forever)
statements.text: Legacy perk Permanence: rest benefits from camping last 50% longer per rank (2 ranks).

statements.title: XP buffs and modifiers (scope: forever)
statements.text: Campfires: you must sit at the camp for 1 minute to get its benefits. Camp features share a 1-hour cooldown, which the Field Guide perk shortens by up to about 25%. Campfires cannot be placed in cities.

statements.title: Rested XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Rested XP doubles kill XP until it runs out. It does not apply to quest or exploration XP.

statements.title: Rested XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Rested XP builds in inns, capital cities and Cozy Sleeping Bag areas, including while logged out there.

statements.title: Rested XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Base rate: 5% of the current level per 8 hours in a resting area. Cap: 150% of a level (1.5 levels), which takes about 10 days to fill.

statements.title: Rested XP (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Logged out anywhere other than a resting area, rested XP builds at a quarter of the inn rate. It also builds while dead or logged out mid-flight. The pool shrinks by the total XP gained from kills (base plus bonus).

statements.title: Death penalties and Hardcore (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Resurrecting at the Spirit Healer costs 25% durability and gives resurrection sickness. Characters level 10 and under are exempt. The wiki applies these Classic values to Forever, but Blizzard has not stated them.

statements.title: Death penalties and Hardcore (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Resurrection sickness cuts stats by 75% and cannot be removed. It lasts 1 minute per level above 10 for levels 11–19, and 10 minutes from level 20.

statements.title: Death penalties and Hardcore (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Dying costs 10% durability on equipped items, and dying again as a ghost costs another 10%. The Spirit Healer adds 25%, which also hits items in bags. Being killed by a player skips the first 10%.

statements.title: Death penalties and Hardcore (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Legacy Reinforce: each rank cuts durability loss on death by 8%, up to 5 ranks (−40%). Legacy The Quick and the Dead: +5% ghost speed per rank, and helpful spells are free for 1 minute per rank after resurrecting (2 ranks).

statements.title: Death penalties and Hardcore (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Might of Stormwind and Warchief's Blessing are now removed on death.

statements.title: Death penalties and Hardcore (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Forever Hardcore was not available at launch. Dead Hardcore characters can move to another ruleset. Progress from other rulesets does not carry into Hardcore, and Hardcore is excluded from shared battlegrounds.

statements.title: Death penalties and Hardcore (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic Hardcore precedent: death is permanent, Soulstone and Reincarnation are disabled, and dead characters can transfer to a normal realm for free.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Forever uses a TBC-style cost model: most of the gold goes on riding training, and learning the skill gives you a mount.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Apprentice Riding: level 40, 100g, +60% speed, first racial mount included. Extra 60% mounts cost 20g each.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Blizzard kept the riding levels at 40 and 60. There is no flying anywhere in Forever.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Discount: Honored with your own race's faction gives 10% off training and racial mounts.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Legacy Bartering (2 ranks) makes vendor items up to 10% cheaper, including mounts. Since a fix in beta it no longer discounts training or repairs.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: No Legacy perk lowers the riding level or the training cost.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Riding another race's mounts requires Exalted with that race. According to the Wowhead guide, the extra skill costs 100g.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Racial vendor mounts are Bind-on-Pickup.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Store mounts (e.g. Cerulean Prideclaw) still need riding skill learned in game.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Tauren Plainsrunning does not add mounted speed. That was reverted on 26 Oct.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: You cannot mount inside Stratholme or in the Warsong Gulch start rooms. You can mount in the named areas of Shen'dralas.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Blizzard's Forever PvP rank list gives cloaks at Rank 3 and mounts at Rank 11. It does not mention a discount at Rank 3.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic Era: level 40, 20g riding skill plus an 80g mount, 60% speed. Level 60: about 1,000g for 100% speed.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic Era discounts: 10% at Honored plus 10% at PvP Rank 3, for 20% combined. There is no extra discount at Revered or Exalted.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic Era race restrictions: Tauren cannot learn Undead Horsemanship or Raptor Riding. Only Dwarves and Gnomes can ride mechanostriders. Mounts from the other faction are never available.

statements.title: Riding skill and mount costs (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic Era PvP mounts: PvP Rank 11 faction mounts (about 90g). The Alterac Valley mounts need Exalted and cost 800g.

statements.title: Class mounts (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Warlock: the level 40 Felsteed quest is given by Strahad Farsan in Ratchet. Since 9 Nov, finishing it also teaches apprentice riding. Anyone who finished it earlier gets the skill by summoning the Felsteed once.

statements.title: Class mounts (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Paladin (Alliance): the level 40 quest "The Tome of Nobility" gives the Warhorse. It is unknown whether it also teaches riding.

statements.title: Class mounts (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: The new Forsaken (Undead) Paladins get their own mount quests. The level 60 charger questline is framed as "Retribution" (Alliance: "Redemption").

statements.title: Class mounts (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic Era: the Warlock Felsteed and Paladin Warhorse come at level 40, and the Dreadsteed and Charger from quests at level 60.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Hearthstone: 10-second cast, 1-hour cooldown, cannot be used while shapeshifted.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: No perk or hotfix changes the Hearthstone. "Second Home", a second hearthstone, exists in game data but is not live.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: You set your hearthstone by talking to an innkeeper. Any innkeeper will replace a lost one.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Frequent Flier (Adventure tree, 1 rank): flight paths cost 50% less and fly 20% faster. Blizzard's own text gives no numbers.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: New ship routes: Stormwind Harbor ↔ Auberdine; Menethil ↔ Southshore ↔ Auberdine; Steamwheedle Port (Tanaris) ↔ Riverglades.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: With a gamepad, you can end a flight early and get off at the next flight point.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: New flight points reported: Farholde Keep (Alliance) and Rog'mar (Horde) in Riverglades; Tainted Foothills and Summit of Eternity in Hyjal. Zephras Isle reportedly has no flight master. No price table has been published.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Skyborne skycutter ships leave Zephras Isle for Dalaran (Alliance) and Mulgore/Thunder Bluff (Horde).

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Mage: city teleports at level 20 (SW, IF, Org, UC) and 30 (Darn, TB); portals at 40 and 50. New: Teleport: Dalaran at level 50, Alliance only.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Druid: Teleport: Moonglade at 10, Aquatic Form at 16, Travel Form at 30 (+40%). Shaman: Ghost Wolf at 20 (+40%), Astral Recall at 30. Hunter: Aspect of the Cheetah at 20 (+30%), Aspect of the Pack at 40.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Legacy Reagent Economy: class spells no longer use vendor reagents, including mage teleport and portal runes.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Movement racials: Tauren Plainsrunning +2% per stack, up to 60%, out of combat and not mounted. Skyborne Skysight +15% for 15 seconds, or +30% while "Charged".

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Horde players are attacked on sight in the open-world city of Dalaran, but can still enter the dungeon.

statements.title: Hearthstone, flights, boats, class travel (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: You discover flight paths by talking to each flight master. Once discovered, you can fly there from any flight master on the same continent, and the reputation discount applies to fares.

statements.title: Dungeon list and level ranges (scope: forever)
statements.text: Each dungeon has a single difficulty; there are no heroic versions. Hundreds of new items were added to new and old dungeons. A new dungeon currency was added (Tarnished Undermine Real).

statements.title: Dungeon list and level ranges (scope: forever)
statements.text: Since 3 Nov, the Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon quests all require level 15.

statements.title: Dungeon list and level ranges (scope: forever)
statements.text: On 17 Nov, Upper Blackrock Spire's health and damage were restored, so it needs a full group again. The Battle for Alterac Valley quests now require level 58. "Agamaggan's Blood" is no longer a dungeon quest.

statements.title: Dungeon list and level ranges (scope: forever)
statements.text: Pix Xizzix gives weekly dungeon quests, which are cleared from your log at the weekly reset.

statements.title: Dungeon list and level ranges (scope: forever)
statements.text: Damage from Drowned City creatures was cut by about 30%.

statements.title: New dungeons in detail (scope: forever)
statements.text: City of Dalaran: you enter through the sewers with a Dalaran Sewer Key. Alliance get it from Emissary Jacques in Southshore ("An Alarming Request"). Horde get it from Magus Wordeen Voidglare in Tarren Mill ("Key to the City" and "Prison Break-In").

statements.title: New dungeons in detail (scope: forever)
statements.text: Dalaran has 8 bosses, including the secret boss Lyn the Ignored. Lyn needs the Black Tome, which drops at the end of Shadowfang Keep.

statements.title: New dungeons in detail (scope: forever)
statements.text: Dalaran has 4 quests per faction. "Heart of Disruption" unlocks the open-world city. Each faction earns about 15,800 XP in total from Dalaran quests (beta figure).

statements.title: New dungeons in detail (scope: forever)
statements.text: Excavation Site: Wetlands: 4 bosses (Saltspine, Shadetooth, the optional Highland Horror, and the final boss Relic Guardian). Alliance have 5 quests, Horde 3. Several bosses apply diseases.

statements.title: New dungeons in detail (scope: forever)
statements.text: The Drowned City is an open-air dungeon with an underwater entrance. Shaper's Terrace uses power crystals collected in Un'Goro. Blackmaw Hold is a furbolg city that also leads to the Barrow Deeps raid.

statements.title: Instance limits and raid lockouts (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: The party leader resets instances from the portrait menu. Warcraft Tavern says you can enter at most 5 instances per hour.

statements.title: Instance limits and raid lockouts (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Blizzard has published no per-hour or per-day instance limit for Forever. The game shows the error "You have entered too many instances recently".

statements.title: Instance limits and raid lockouts (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic in 2020 limited players to 30 instances per day per realm, on top of 5 per hour.

statements.title: Instance limits and raid lockouts (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: The 30-per-day cap was removed around the TBC Classic pre-patch in May 2021. No source shows it returning in 2023.

statements.title: Instance limits and raid lockouts (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic today: 10 instances per hour on a rolling hour. Players quote support article 10994, which could not be read without logging in.

statements.title: Instance limits and raid lockouts (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic Hardcore: most dungeons lock for 24 hours per character.

statements.title: Instance limits and raid lockouts (forever where known, else classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic raid lockouts: Molten Core 7 days, Onyxia 5 days, Zul'Gurub and AQ20 3 days.

statements.title: Group finder and summoning (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: There is no automatic dungeon queue and no teleport into dungeons. The LFG tool works like Classic's: you post or browse a list.

statements.title: Group finder and summoning (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: The LFG tool shows eligibility for mixed-level groups and has a "Show All Level Ranges" option.

statements.title: Group finder and summoning (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: LFG listings can carry playstyle tags (Learning, Relaxed, Competitive, Carry Offered), roles and a "new players welcome" flag.

statements.title: Group finder and summoning (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Meeting stones cannot summon. The Warlock's Ritual of Summoning, which needs two more party members at the site, is the only way to summon.

statements.title: Group finder and summoning (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Players are pooled across the whole ruleset in a region, so no separate cross-realm feature exists.

statements.title: Legacy system rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Legacy is account-wide progression with three parts: Challenges earn points, Trees spend them on perks, and a Reward track gives cosmetics.

statements.title: Legacy system rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Legacy unlocks with the account's first point, usually when a character reaches level 25. It can also unlock at 150 in a non-gathering primary profession or by exploring the whole world map. The hotkey is Y.

statements.title: Legacy system rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: There are 65 challenges, each worth 1 point. Points are shared by all non-Hardcore characters on the account, but each character spends them separately.

statements.title: Legacy system rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Each character can spend at most 16 points at launch. Blizzard plans to raise the cap but has given no date. No hotfix up to 17 Nov changed it.

statements.title: Legacy system rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: A single character can earn at most 29 points without alts. This is a limit on earning, not on spending.

statements.title: Legacy system rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Each challenge, and its point, can be earned only once per account.

statements.title: Legacy reward track and Legacy respec (scope: forever)
statements.text: The reward track counts points earned, not points spent. Rewards: 15 points, Ironforge Air Rifle toy; 25, Spectral Bear Cub pet; 40, Spectral Bear Tabard; 55, Reins of the Spectral Bear mount (100% speed).

statements.title: Legacy reward track and Legacy respec (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rewards are collected from Innkeeper Wiley in Ratchet.

statements.title: Legacy reward track and Legacy respec (scope: forever)
statements.text: The Spectral Bear mount reportedly needs level 60 and Journeyman Riding.

statements.title: Legacy reward track and Legacy respec (scope: forever)
statements.text: Legacy perks are reset at your own class trainer in a major city.

statements.title: Legacy reward track and Legacy respec (scope: forever)
statements.text: A Legacy reset cost 10g in beta. Datamined price steps: 10, 20, 40, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 425 and 500g, said to drop one step every 7 days. Not confirmed on live servers.

statements.title: Talents, dual spec, respec (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Talents start at level 10. Each class has three trees. One-point milestone talents sit at 11, 21 and 31 points in a tree, plus a new one at 16.

statements.title: Talents, dual spec, respec (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: You get one point per level from 10, for 51 at level 60. Talented brings them earlier but does not raise the 51 total.

statements.title: Talents, dual spec, respec (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: The talent trees changed a lot in the 3 Nov pre-launch notes, so talent calculators built during beta may be out of date.

statements.title: Talents, dual spec, respec (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Dual specialization unlocks at level 40.

statements.title: Talents, dual spec, respec (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Guides and the wiki say dual spec costs 50g once, with free switching. No Blizzard post states the price.

statements.title: Talents, dual spec, respec (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: You respec at your own class trainer, and this also covers Legacy talents.

statements.title: Talents, dual spec, respec (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Live respec cost: the first is 1g, then the price rises to a 50g cap. Players report steps of 1, 5 and 10g and a roughly weekly drop back down.

statements.title: Talents, dual spec, respec (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: The 1-silver respec was for beta only.

statements.title: Talents, dual spec, respec (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: No free respec exists, and no perk makes respecs cheaper.

statements.title: Talents, dual spec, respec (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Original WoW respec prices were 1g, 5g, 10g and so on, capped at 50g.

statements.title: Class changes and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Training every class ability from 1 to 60 costs about 206–207g for every class.

statements.title: Class changes and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Several former talent buffs became baseline, for example Blessing of Kings, Divine Spirit and Consecration (for every Paladin at level 20).

statements.title: Class changes and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Hunter: Aimed Shot is baseline at 20, traps can be used in combat, and pets scale with the hunter's gear.

statements.title: Class changes and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Warrior: Victory Rush at 20 and Tactical Mastery baseline at 14. The separate weapon specialisation talents were merged into Weaponmaster.

statements.title: Class changes and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Druid: out-of-combat res (Revive) at 12, Omen of Clarity baseline at 20. Mage: Frostfire Bolt at 40, plus the new "Comprehension" scroll skill. Shaman: buff totems last 5 minutes, weapon imbues 60 minutes. Priest: Fear Ward and Devouring Plague for every priest at 20.

statements.title: Class changes and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rogue: can use one-handed axes; Sap no longer breaks stealth. Warlock: pets scale with the warlock's stats, and trainer costs were cut to offset Grimoire purchases. Paladin: Holy Strike at 6, Seal of Fury at 10.

statements.title: Professions (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: You can have 2 primary professions plus all 3 secondary ones. The skill cap stays at 300.

statements.title: Professions (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Blacksmithing, Engineering and Leatherworking have specialisations, learned through quests.

statements.title: Professions (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Profession trainers and gathering nodes exist in starting zones. Since 5 Nov, Zephras Isle vendors sell apprentice profession bags.

statements.title: Professions (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: A creature can only be skinned once. Some Blacksmithing and Leatherworking recipes drop in dungeons.

statements.title: Professions (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Skill requirements changed: Tanning Rack now 125 (was 140); Journeyman Campfire Kit now needs Cooking 90 (was 140); Coarse Grinding Stone gives skill-ups up to 90.

statements.title: Professions (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Vendors now pay less for some Bind-on-Pickup crafted armour, to stop crafting purely for vendor gold.

statements.title: Professions (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Moving secondary professions from 150 to 225 needs Expert books: Cooking from Shandrina (Alliance) or Wulan (Horde); First Aid from Deneb Walker or Balai Lok'Wein; Fishing from Old Man Heming. The wiki says these still work this way in Forever.

statements.title: Weapon skills (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Weapon skill works the same as in Classic. The tooltip now shows its effect against each target level.

statements.title: Weapon skills (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: The maximum for weapon skill and defense is 5 × character level.

statements.title: Weapon skills (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Weapon skill bonuses on items are much smaller (e.g. Edgemaster's +7 is now +1). The racial weapon specialisations were reworked into crit bonuses, but the final live form is disputed.

statements.title: Weapon skills (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Weapon masters are the same NPCs as in Classic. Each weapon costs 10s to learn; polearms need level 20 and cost 1g.

statements.title: Weapon skills (forever / classic_fallback)
statements.text: Rogues can learn one-handed axes and Druids can learn polearms.

statements.title: Economy rules relevant to levelling (scope: forever)
statements.text: Accounts suspected of buying or selling gold can be put on a "Temporary Economy Hold": no trading, mail, guild bank or auction house until the review ends.

statements.title: Economy rules relevant to levelling (scope: forever)
statements.text: Blizzard removes illicit gold and suspends or closes accounts of botters and gold buyers.

statements.title: Economy rules relevant to levelling (scope: forever)
statements.text: A cut in the auction house minimum deposit from 1 silver to 1 copper was announced, pulled on 12 Nov and rescheduled for 17 Nov. It is not confirmed live.

open_questions.text: **Client and API identifiers.** No public source confirms `profile-forever-eu`, the `_forever_` folder, or a wago.tools product code. wago.tools returned 403. Verify locally against the client and the Battle.net API.

**Talents from client data.** I found no datamined TraitTree/TraitNode tables for 1.60.x. Exact node layout, row gating and rank counts per class need direct DB2 access, because the Wowhead calculator renders with JavaScript only.
**Instance limits.** Blizzard has published nothing for Forever: per hour (5 or 10?), per day (any cap?), and per account or per character.
**Raid lockouts.** Duration, reset weekday per region, and whether the 10/20/40-player raids share lockouts are all unknown. Raids open 9 Dec.
**Rested XP in Forever.** The rate, the outside-inn rate and the cap come from guides, not Blizzard. The exact absolute value of the Well Rested perk is also unconfirmed.
**Group XP.** Are the 3- and 4-player multipliers and the raid XP penalty the same as Classic? Was the overworld zero-XP-in-groups report a bug, and is it fixed?
**Mob XP formula.** What is the exact formula behind the 4–20% cut for green mobs? Were the ZD or grey-level tables changed? Were elite or instance multipliers changed?
**Dungeon XP numbers.** What are the exact live kill and quest XP values compared with Classic after all the changes (−design cut, +20%, +50%, −50% quest bonus)?
**Death penalties.** Durability percentages and resurrection sickness duration are not stated by Blizzard for Forever. Hardcore death rules and the Hardcore launch date are also unknown.

**Riding:** one general skill or one per creature type; discount ladder (Honored only, or 5–20%); whether the PvP Rank 3 discount exists; whether the Skyborne discount bug is fixed; whether the Paladin level 40 quest teaches riding; level 60 class epic mount requirements; Rank 11 PvP mount price.
**Live respec ladder.** The talent respec steps and decay period, the dual-spec price (50g?), whether the fee is shared across both specs, and the Legacy respec price are all unconfirmed.

**Legacy:** when the 16-point cap will rise; what the 6 placeholder slots will hold; whether Second Home and Personal Banking will go live; the exact tier gates; the 12 Hardcore challenges; the Spectral Bear mount's level and riding requirement.

**Profession training costs.** No Forever source states them; they are assumed to be Classic. It is unconfirmed whether the secondary Expert books and Artisan quests are unchanged, whether healing potions moved to First Aid, and whether the Mage "Comprehension" skill has caps.

**Flights and boats.** There is no official flight fare table or flight point list, and no confirmation that the Classic zeppelin routes are unchanged. It is unknown where Teleport: Dalaran is learned.
**Dungeon entry levels.** The live minimum entry levels per dungeon (e.g. Excavation 24 or 26) need datamining (LFGDungeons / Map). UBRS group size is also unconfirmed.
**Other:** Is there a WoW Token? Did the auction house deposit cut go live on 17 Nov? Is Forever available in China?
**Not readable for this report:** Icy Veins, Mobalytics and MassivelyOP pages (403). Their claims appear only from search snippets and are marked accordingly.
